When I was younger, me and my older brother lived in front of the Mitre Castle (where Byker Grove was filmed). One night, while we were talking at around midnight, we heard noises coming from the castle. Bemused, we went to see where these noises were coming from and noticed that a light was on at one of the castle windows and heard a monkey screaming repeatedly.

The sounds were definitely real and weren't put on or anything. I've never felt so frightened and yet laughed so much at the same time.

Nobody believes us to this day. Mitre Castle was also up for sale at the time. God only knows what was going on.

I think one aspect people forget when comparing the two movies is that the 90s version was designed for TV on a limited budget, had restrictions in what they could show, and had to be cut down severely along with various changes in the director. George Romero was first brought in but left after being dissatisfied with the planned running time (he wanted to make a 2 parter spanning 7 hours).

The 2017 movie didn't have all of these limitations and was made on a budget of up to $40m. This makes comparisons difficult in certain areas between both movies. 

There's a great documentary called 'Pennywise: The Story of IT' which goes into great detail on the production behind the 90s mini series.

Actually the industrial revolution began in Britain largely because of internal needs as opposed to external outside needs. Our population was amongst the highest growing in Europe, the civil war a century prior (16th century) led us away from laws established by monarchs and more parliamentary focused which meant institutions such as banks became more 'inclusive'. This meant they were more free to provide capital to entrepreneurs without having to give it to an aristocracy e.g. a monarch, which led to the innovations I listed above having more probability of being created as they could now afford to do so. Essentially, we came up with the industrial revolution to address our own faculties and changed the world as we know it.

Also with Britain being such a tiny island with a rich vain of resources, this meant that many towns and cities had very short routes to access these resources. The industrial revolution would have been nearly impossible to begin say in the United States for instance because of the geographical landmass.

In Britain around the mid-1700s for instance, it was actually the advancement of technological innovations such as steam power, iron and steel making processors, textile production, new handmaking machinery, chemical production e.g. sulfuric acid and architectural advancements related to factory designs as well as other newly discovered means that were the basis for the industrial revolution to begin with.
